n: Chapter 34 contrasts Israel’s selfish leaders with the Lord, the true Shepherd. Jesus drew on this chapter when he called himself the Good Shepherd.

f.w: the word of the LORD came unto me

n: “Shepherds” in the ancient Near East meant kings and leaders. Woe to Israel’s shepherds who feed themselves instead of the flock!

f.w: the shepherds of Israel
should not the shepherds feed the flocks?

n: They eat the best, wear the wool, and slaughter the fattest sheep, but never care for the flock. Leadership became a way to profit.

f.w: Ye eat the fat

n: They haven’t strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bandaged the injured, brought back strays, or searched for the lost. Instead they ruled harshly. This is a clear description of what true ministering looks like.

f.w: neither have ye sought that which was lost
with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them

n: Without a real shepherd, the sheep scattered and became prey to wild animals—the nations.

f.w: scattered, because there is no shepherd

n: God’s sheep wandered over every mountain and were scattered across the earth, and no one searched for them.

f.w: none did search or seek after them

n: So, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

f.w: ye shepherds

n: God swears: because his flock became prey while the shepherds fed only themselves…

f.w: my flock
f.g: God repeatedly calls Israel his own flock.

n: …shepherds, listen!

f.w: hear the word of the LORD

n: God is against these shepherds. He will hold them accountable for his sheep and remove them from leadership, rescuing his flock from their mouths.

f.w: I will require my flock at their hand

n: Then the great promise: “I, even I, will search for my sheep and seek them out.” The Lord himself will come as Shepherd. Latter-day Saints recognize this Shepherd as Jehovah, Jesus Christ.

f.w: I, even I, will both search my sheep

n: As a shepherd gathers his scattered flock, God will rescue them from every place they were scattered on that dark, cloudy day—the day of Jerusalem’s fall.

f.w: the cloudy and dark day

n: He will bring them out of the nations, gather them, and pasture them on Israel’s mountains by its streams—the promise of gathering.

f.w: gather them from the countries

n: Good grazing land and secure folds on Israel’s high mountains—the picture recalls Psalm 23.

f.w: I will feed them in a good pasture

n: “I myself will feed my flock and give them rest.”

f.w: I will cause them to lie down

n: God will do everything the bad shepherds failed to do: seek the lost, bring back the strays, bandage the hurt, strengthen the weak. But the fat and strong who exploit others he will judge.

f.w: I will seek that which was lost
I will feed them with judgment
f.g: Or “I will shepherd them with justice.”

n: Now God speaks to the flock itself: he will judge between sheep and sheep, rams and goats. Jesus later used this image of separating sheep and goats.

f.w: between the rams and the he goats

n: Some sheep not only eat the best grass but trample the rest; they drink clear water and muddy what’s left. Selfishness isn’t limited to leaders.

f.w: tread down with your feet the residue of your pastures

n: The weaker sheep must eat what was trampled and drink what was muddied.

f.w: they eat that which ye have trodden
f.g: The poor live with the leftovers of the powerful.

n: God himself will judge between the fat and the lean.

f.w: the fat cattle and between the lean cattle

n: The strong pushed the weak aside with shoulder and horn until they were scattered.

f.w: pushed all the diseased with your horns

n: God will save his flock so they are no longer prey, and he will judge between sheep.

f.w: will I save my flock

n: God will set one shepherd over them—“my servant David.” David had died centuries earlier, so this points to a future king from David’s line: the Messiah. Christians see its fulfillment in Jesus Christ, the Son of David.

f.w: one shepherd
my servant David

n: The Lord will be their God, and David his prince among them. God and his anointed rule together.

f.w: a prince among them

n: He will make a “covenant of peace” and rid the land of dangerous animals, so his sheep can sleep safely even in wilderness and forest.

f.w: a covenant of peace
cause the evil beasts to cease

n: His people and the area around his holy hill will be a blessing; rain will come in its season—“showers of blessing.”

f.w: there shall be showers of blessing
my hill

n: Trees and fields will be fruitful, and they will be safe. They’ll know God when he breaks their yoke and frees them from those who enslaved them.

f.w: broken the bands of their yoke

n: No longer prey to nations or beasts, they will live in safety with no one to make them afraid.

f.w: none shall make them afraid

n: God will give them a land renowned for its crops—or, as some read it, a “plant of renown” pointing to the Messiah, the righteous Branch. Hunger and shame will end.

f.w: a plant of renown
f.g: Possibly a famous planting or harvest; many see a messianic hint.

n: They will know that the Lord their God is with them and that Israel is his people.

f.w: I the LORD their God am with them

n: “You are my flock, the sheep of my pasture; you are people, and I am your God.” A tender close: God’s care for his people is personal.

f.w: the flock of my pasture
